clue.text: Show forbearance, despite vile, vile dental work

indicators.note: dental work suggests reshaping, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a truly awful bout of dentistry with patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges VILE, VILE and DENTAL together; 'despite' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tolerating other people's ways without interference, which is a kind of forbearance.

clue.text: I go green before giddiness

indicators.note: placed in front of what follows, so the green colour comes first

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns pale green just before feeling dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic term for green, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of spinning dizziness, a synonym for giddiness.

clue.text: A road in the distance

parts.note: a way is a road or path

explanation.surface: A road stretching off into the far distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far off is distant, so the adverb and the phrase are synonyms.

clue.text: Exceptional Sudanese ballerina

indicators.note: exceptional suggests out of the ordinary, so the letters of the following word leave their usual order

explanation.surface: A remarkable dancer from Sudan is praised.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, the French term for one.

clue.text: Conclusion causing uproar in England

indicators.note: the noise sits inside the country abbreviation, as 'in' says

parts.note: a din is a loud uproar

explanation.surface: A finish that provokes a furore across England.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the final part, a synonym for conclusion.

clue.text: What bookshops retail? True, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding words could take another form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what bookshops sell, answered with a wry remark about truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'What bookshops' borrows the verb from the anagram fodder 'retail', so the clue is close to an all-in-one; 'perhaps' rearranges RETAIL and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Books and written works are what bookshops sell, so literature is their stock.

clue.text: Painter takes vehicle to embankment

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a dyke is an embankment against flooding

explanation.surface: An artist drives a van down to the sea wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... to' simply joins VAN and DYKE in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony van Dyck, often spelt Vandyke, was a Flemish portrait artist.

clue.text: One in anti-ritual movement is severely practical

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters, as 'in' says
movement means the letters of the hyphenated word are moved around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A member of an anti-ritual campaign is very down-to-earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' rearranges ANTIRITUAL and 'in' places I inside it; 'movement' poses as a campaign group.
explanation.definitionFit: Utilitarian describes things designed purely for function rather than beauty, so it is starkly practical.

clue.text: Destined to be a priest, obviously

definitions.meaning: a priest has evidently been admitted to holy orders

explanation.surface: Someone fated to enter the priesthood, as plainly anyone could see.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordained means both decreed in advance by fate and formally admitted to the clergy.

clue.text: People leave apartment block out of principle

indicators.note: the people depart from the building, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a tenement is a block of flats
men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: Residents move out of their flats as a matter of conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes MEN out of TENEMENT; 'out of principle' tempts as a phrase, but 'out of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a synonym for principle.

clue.text: It repairs a fracture in moulded statue

definitions.meaning: a rigid casing put round a broken limb so the bone can mend
a sculpture copy made by pouring material into a mould

explanation.surface: Something is mending a crack inside a sculpted figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster cast is both the hard medical casing for a broken bone and a sculptural copy made from a mould.

clue.text: Large, dry hideout

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: A big, arid hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' looks like an adjective but is the verb, as in airing washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den or a criminal's hiding place.

clue.text: Mint money for the monarch

parts.note: a penny is a coin, a piece of money
royal means belonging to or fit for the sovereign

explanation.surface: Freshly struck coins are made for the king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' poses as the verb for making coins, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a small aromatic plant of the mint family.

clue.text: Just manage to prepare house for re-surfacing?

definitions.meaning: to succeed narrowly, getting there by the skin of one's teeth
read literally, stripping old paint off a dwelling before redecorating

explanation.surface: Barely coping while getting the house ready for redecoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to win or finish narrowly, and read literally it describes stripping a dwelling's walls before repainting.

clue.text: Money on the nail

parts.note: paying on the nail means paying at once, so this is payment made immediately in ready money

explanation.definitionFit: Spot cash is payment made immediately on delivery, which is what paying on the nail means.

clue.text: Swear that a non-drinker is French

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: Declaring that an abstainer is from France.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare solemnly that something is true, as on oath.

clue.text: Commercial area of Newry, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the business district at a city's centre
Newry is a town in County Down, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A question about the shopping district of a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newry lies in County Down, so it is a 'Down town'; the 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtown means a city's central business district, and Newry is literally a town in County Down.

clue.text: Beguile live-in lover endlessly on return

indicators.note: going back means the shortened word is read right to left
without its final letter, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a partner is someone one lives with

explanation.surface: Seducing a cohabiting lover again and again when they come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts PARTNER to PARTNE, and 'on return' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to lure or trick someone, close to beguiling them.

clue.text: Terrible strain put on a leading Russian lady

indicators.note: terrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dreadful stress weighs on a prominent Russian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges STRAIN, recalling Ivan the Terrible; 'put on' sets A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or an empress of Russia, its foremost lady.

clue.text: He cadges from Romany writer with little compunction

parts.note: George Borrow wrote books on Romany life, such as Lavengro and The Romany Rye
er is a small hesitation, a slight qualm voiced aloud

explanation.surface: A scrounger takes from a Gypsy author without much guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow was a 19th-century English writer on Romany life; ER is read as a faint hesitation, a tiny scruple.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes things on loan, often a scrounger, is one who cadges.

clue.text: Join the debate and entrance utterly

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so the words are to be heard

parts.note: a way in is an entrance

explanation.surface: Taking part in an argument and being completely spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' poses as 'completely' but signals speech; 'entrance' is the noun, not the verb to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh in is to contribute forcefully to a discussion.

clue.text: Such a deposit on motor upsets VIP

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a nob is a person of high rank

explanation.surface: A deposit on a car's engine annoys an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon builds up as a sooty residue in engines, a common deposit.

clue.text: Mistress has to teach liane composition

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A housekeeper must instruct someone about writing an essay on a climbing vine.
explanation.walkthrough: A liane is a tropical climbing plant; 'composition' rearranges TEACH and LIANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the mistress of a large house or castle.

clue.text: Pass is needed in the Victoria and Albert

indicators.note: the word goes inside the two abbreviations, as 'in' says

parts.note: V is an abbreviation for Victoria
A is an abbreviation for Albert

explanation.surface: A ticket is required to enter the V&A museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victoria and Albert is a London museum; its initials V and A surround IS, with 'needed in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement allowing entry to a country, a kind of pass.

clue.text: It's fish for tea

definitions.meaning: British slang for a cup of tea

explanation.surface: A family announces what is on the menu at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is both a freshwater fish related to trout and an informal British word for tea.

clue.text: Bearing money, I travel in Ireland

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
L stands for pound, from libra
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Carrying cash, someone journeys round Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place found 'in Ireland'; L is the old symbol for pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a town and county in the north-west of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: Commotion makes brother unionist laugh

parts.note: U is an abbreviation for Unionist in Northern Irish politics
ha ha is a laugh

explanation.surface: A sibling who supports the union bursts out laughing and causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Appeared to have built a porch

definitions.meaning: came on stage or into a room
read literally, to have constructed a doorway

explanation.surface: Someone showed up after constructing a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means arrived in a noticeable way, and read literally it describes constructing a way into a house.
